decisions.reason: The classic lever handle line builds directly on the firm's core design and fixing know-how, and architectural hardware sells over long lifecycles, so withdrawing it after four years is unlikely.
This multi-model handle family rests on established competencies and certified systems, so the firm can read market feedback and refine it within the range rather than drop it.
This single design sits close to the core offer and is easy to keep in the range, though its narrower scope makes a later range clean-up somewhat more likely, as happened with Product D.
The lever handle family adds system breadth and draws on the firm's existing knowledge base, which supports keeping it as a long-lifecycle range item.
The flagship electronic access system fits the strategic move toward digital building organization, and in-house R&D gives the firm the capacity to keep developing it.
